title: What is SPECT/CT (Single-Photon Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography)?
text: Single-Photon Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (SPECT/CT) is a radionuclide examination technique, which provides a stratified image of human anatomical structures due to the distribution of radionuclides in human body. Radiopharmaceuticals are used for this (the most commonly used is technetium).

title: How does it differ from Scintigraphy and Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (PET/CT)?
text: Unlike Scintigraphy, Single-Photon Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (SPECT/CT) allows for 3D imaging; and unlike Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (PET/CT), due to the injected radioactive isotope, as a result of physical interactions in the body, certain features of only one gamma-ray off and image acquisition.

title: Where is Single-Photon Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (SPECT/CT) used?
text:
• In cardiology (assessment of myocardial perfusion);
  • In neurology;
  • In urology (dynamic-static nephroscintigraphy);
  • In pulmonology;
  • When diagnosing brain tumors;
  • During breast cancer scintigraphy;
  • During osteosynthesis (detection of primary և secondary bone cancer);
  • During liver and spleen scintigraphy;
  • During thyroid gland and glandulae parathyreoideae scintigraphy.

title: When is this examination be conducted?
text: The examination is conducted according to the doctor's instructions when there is a suspicion of primary or secondary skeletal infection, as well as when there is a suspicion of pathology in any of the above-mentioned aspects.
